_comment: Every coefficient the engine uses. If a number affects behaviour it lives here, never in C#. One top-level section per engine packet, so two packets can never fight over the same key. Read it through Agora.Core.Tuning.EngineTuning — never parse it yourself. Values are M2 defaults; the simulation harness tunes them against real runs.

blocs._comment: Packet 1. Blocs are wealth x education x age (3 x 5 x 4 = 60 per district). Weights say how much a bloc cares; ideals say what it wants. Both are derived from composition, then nudged by lived metrics.

parties._comment: Packet 2. EU parties split, merge, die below deathVoteShareThreshold across two consecutive elections, and revive if their core grievance resurges (plan section 3). NA party-level lifecycle is handled in `factions`. deathVoteShareThreshold sits below `fringe.baseCeiling` on purpose: a party the fringe ceiling is holding down has not been rejected by voters, and must not be killed by the suppression itself. incumbencyDecayPerTerm is per TERM, so it was rescaled with the 1-year term to preserve its per-year shape. anchoredSpreadSigma is the generation jitter for a catalog entry flagged isAnchored — the four NA brands, which are fixed institutions rather than generated ones. It is far below archetypeSpreadSigma because 0.35 on a [-1,+1] axis flips the sign of every axis except the defining one, which is fine for inventing a party and wrong for one the player already has expectations about.

factions._comment: Packet 3. NA theme: each party holds 2-4 factions with their own demographic support, demands and leader. The dominant faction writes the party platform each cycle.

affinity._comment: Packet 4. Affinity = issue proximity + incumbency + mandate performance + event modifiers + habitual loyalty + seeded noise. Noise is clamped so one tail draw cannot decide an election. habitualLoyalty was cut with the move to 1-year terms: loyalty decays from the last election at loyaltyDecayPerMonth, so over 12 months it now only falls to ~0.79 of its value instead of ~0.38 over four years, and the old 0.35 made the electorate far too sticky. softmaxTemperature came down from 0.35 because it, not the lived-metric pipeline, was what made every district vote the same: two districts set as far apart as the sensors can see them swung 4.8 points at 0.35 and 11.0 at 0.15, and a middle-income mid-education bloc had an ideological range of only 0.126 points across the whole nine-party field. Nothing crosses electionsPr.thresholdShare or parties.deathVoteShareThreshold at the new value, and the lowest share any bloc gives any party is 2.4%, well clear of minPartyShare. eventModifierWeight came down with it: temperature amplifies every term equally, and at 0.25 one aligned severity-5 event was already worth about twice a centrist bloc's entire ideological span, so sharpening without trimming would have made the centre chase headlines and nothing else.

turnout._comment: Packet 5. Turnout scales with happiness and education and can flip close races. Child and teen multipliers are 0 — that is how minors are disenfranchised; the blocs still exist.

polling._comment: Packet 6. Published polls under-sample low-education, low-turnout districts. The harness asserts the DIRECTION of that error, never the magnitude, so these two bias values must stay positive. 9 weeks is a shade over the 2-month campaign flag, so the poll season opens a few days before the flag does — the same slack the old 26-weeks-vs-6-months pairing had.

electionsPr._comment: Packet 7. EU theme: proportional list seats, 1-year terms, 5% threshold, modified Sainte-Lague with a 1.4 first divisor. snapElectionMinMonthsSinceLast is deliberately well under termYears*12 — at 12 it equalled a whole term and made snap elections structurally impossible.

electionsFptp._comment: Packet 8. NA theme: one seat per district plus a directly elected mayor, 1-year terms. primariesEnabled is an open decision (plan section 14) — leave it false.

coalitions._comment: Packet 9. Formation ranks candidate coalitions by ideological closeness and size; stability decays monthly and takes shocks from failed mandates and severe events. Falling below collapseThreshold triggers a snap election. Note that stabilityDecayPerMonth carries stabilityInitial down to collapseThreshold only after 50 months — several terms under the 1-year term — so governments now fall from shocks, essentially never from decay alone.

mandates._comment: Packet 10. Mandates come from real measured deficits and are scored monthly against the live snapshot. Fulfilled raises happiness and legitimacy; defied lowers both and can trigger unrest. The player is never punished beyond a sanctioned effect. horizonMonths must not exceed the term length: a mandate that outlives the government that issued it is abandoned unscored at the next election, and `fringe` reads defiance as its largest failure signal.

catalog._comment: Packet 11. Curated real history 1990 onward, then procedural mode. jitterEnabled and the procedural block are open decisions (plan section 14) — the keys exist so nothing hardcodes them, but do not build past the ratified shape.

scheduler._comment: Packet 12. The monthly tick and everything hung off it. snapshotRetention is an open decision (proposed 25) — keep the newest N and nothing cleverer. The three lifecycleTickMonths/lifecycleCheckIntervalMonths keys stay at 12 under the 1-year term: they now fire once per term rather than a quarter as often, and a shorter interval would thrash the ballot. If churn is too high, lower the per-cycle probabilities, not this interval.

indices._comment: Packet 13. Derived indices, all normalised to [0,1] so the dashboard can render them on one scale.

effects._comment: Packet 14. The closed effect registry. Every entry names a real member of Game.Areas.DistrictModifierType or Game.City.CityModifierType (Scout 0001 section 3) and declares scope, magnitude cap, duration cap and a fallback. An effectId not listed here does not exist. The two terminal fallbacks carry an empty fallbackEffectId so the sink cannot loop.

fringe._comment: Packet 15. NA/FPTP only — the 'weak third parties' half of the ratified NA system (plan section 3). A party with isMajor false is pinned at baseCeiling until the majors have failed unlockConsecutiveTerms terms running; the ceiling then opens toward maxCeiling in proportion to how badly they failed, how long the failure has run, and how aggrieved the city is on that specific fringe party's own core issue. The EU proportional threshold (electionsPr.thresholdShare) is deliberately untouched — multiparty PR is supposed to have viable small parties. The three signal weights must sum to 1.

stories._comment: Packet 16. The story cycle: each cycle drafts storiesPerCycle stories of eventsPerStory events (one major, two minors), and they resolve cycleMonths later. cycleMonths is a MONTH count and there is deliberately no day-based alternative — one in-game day IS one calendar month (TimeSettingsData.m_DaysPerYear = 12), so a mid-month reading returns the byte-identical snapshot taken at month start and every metric and delta check would be provably unmeasurable. Forcing a fresh mid-month sample instead would make the reading depend on which 128-frame tick crossed the threshold, which is a non-deterministic input and forbidden by non-negotiable #3. Full argument in docs/plans/0004-event-system-rework.md.
stories._severityComment: Mandatory/Major/Minor is a PROJECTION of the existing 1-5 severity integer, never a stored enum. majorSeverityThreshold is deliberately equal to catalog.majorSeverityThreshold: 'major' already has exactly one definition, shared by EventScheduler.IsMajor, CoalitionStability and the alert lane, and a second number for one concept would drift on the next tuning pass.
stories._reuseComment: reuseCooldownMonths is a DURATION and must stay well under liveCatalogSize / (storiesPerCycle * eventsPerStory) * cycleMonths — about 13 months at these values. Re-use was originally gated on 'anything the archive remembers', which is only sound while archiveRetention * eventsPerStory < liveCatalogSize; at 40 and 3 that names 120 slots over a ~40-event live catalog, so the pool emptied around month 14 and then never refilled — nothing drafted, so nothing resolved, so nothing archived, so nothing was ever released. Mandatory events ignore the cooldown: a mandatory trigger is a statement about the city right now.
stories._breadthComment: effects.stackingMode is 'sum' with maxStackedPerModifier 4, so six story events several of which share a modifier would hit that limit and SILENTLY DROP the fifth. Capping breadth at draft time enforces it where it can be reasoned about rather than discovered in the ledger. Keep this below effects.maxStackedPerModifier.

power._comment: Packet 17. The political-power currency that gates an override and punishes debt. successGain and overrideCost are keyed by the DERIVED story tier (see stories.mandatorySeverityThreshold), not by a stored field. failureLossRatio is below 1 on purpose: failing should cost less than succeeding pays, so the economy rewards engagement rather than punishing it. A manual self-declared outcome is capped at the MINOR rate whatever the tier — otherwise a one-word justification mints the mandatory award.
